criteria.check: regulatory.config.json present; every inclusion declared default/customised/not-applicable; operator identity confirmed by a named person
criteria.notes: Silence is not acceptance. The declaration exists to force Trigger A (whose legal identity is behind this surface) to be answered explicitly rather than assumed to be ours — the assumption that puts CAS's ABN on a distributor's product. 'not-applicable' requires a reason, not a shrug.

criteria.check: Every declared inclusion URL resolves 200, is not a dead '#' anchor, and contains no REPLACE marker
criteria.notes: The highest-value check in the set and purely mechanical, so a waiver could only ever be an excuse. Catches the real failure, which is not a MISSING policy but a PUBLISHED placeholder sitting under a tickbox that says 'I agree to the Privacy Policy'. Found in production on DealFindrs 2026-05-26. Vacuous (auto-passes) when #44 declares everything not-applicable, so it costs nothing where it does not apply.

criteria.check: Voice consent reconciled: product privacy copy does not contradict the vendor consent modal, and the policy that modal links to exists
criteria.notes: ElevenLabs shows its own modal before every call ('...sharing of my communications with third-party service providers'), and @caistech/elevenlabs-convai never configures consent text, so EVERY voice product in the portfolio currently shows the vendor default. The modal is not wrong — ElevenLabs is genuinely a third-party processor — so the failure is product copy that contradicts it, plus the linked policy 404ing. Live on Kira and BucketLyst.
